summary: Richard Jolly profiles Cole Palmer, who moved from Manchester City to Chelsea for £42.5m and has become a pivotal starter and penalty taker. He discusses his calm temperament, his 4-4 draw penalty against his old club, his decision to leave City, and the prospect of an England senior call-up. He jokes that the traffic is the worst part of moving south.
one_line: Cole Palmer reflects on his rapid rise since leaving Manchester City for Chelsea, his penalty-taking composure and his possible England debut.
key_facts: Cole Palmer moved from Manchester City to Chelsea in 2023, swapping south Manchester (his native Wythenshawe) for the South; he says the most annoying thing is the traffic.
Palmer scored an injury-time penalty for Chelsea against City on Sunday, completing a 4-4 draw, and marked it with a shrug.
He spent 15 years at City and said celebrating a 95th-minute equaliser would have been disrespectful.
Palmer scored in the Community Shield and European Super Cup for City, and against Arsenal and Tottenham for Chelsea.
He took the penalty at Turf Moor to open his Chelsea account and decided afterwards: 'I'll take them'.
Palmer said he would be willing to come off the bench as a specialist penalty taker in a shootout.
His last miss was as a substitute in the shootout when City lost the 2019 FA Youth Cup final to Liverpool.
Chelsea paid £42.5m after City decided Palmer could only leave on a permanent deal; Brighton, Burnley and RB Leipzig had been interested in a loan.
Palmer is 21 and was part of England Under-21s' European Championship win in 2023.
He said he wasn't thinking of an England call-up when he first went to Chelsea.
He judged that departures including Mason Mount, Kai Havertz, Christian Pulisic and Joao Felix opened chances in attacking midfield.
As a boy, his mother banned him from playing in the garden because he kept breaking her pipes.
An England debut could follow in the next week.
